Scaroni explains Cardinale’s ‘long-term’ project and why stadium is ‘fundamental’ for success

  • Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paolo Scaroni has insisted that AC Milan have a long-term project under Gerry Cardinale, for which the stadium is a vital component.

As we wrote about at length last night, Cardinale has substantial plans to help get Milan back towards the top end of European football. The fresh ‘MSE’ holding manufacturer is the latest development, while the Generali Stadium was recently unveiled, and other projects like the NBA Europe team are ongoing.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that it is all part of a mission to try and make the Rossoneri brand more than just a football club. Scaroni has been the face of the stadium project for many years, and he was a guest at a sports talk organised by RCS and entitled ‘Attracting foreign capital and enhancing the system for a real relaunch’.

He spoke alongside Giovanni Carnevali (CEO and General Manager of Juventus), Giuseppe Marotta (President and CEO of Inter) and Ezio Maria Simonelli, (President of the Lega Calcio Serie A). His words are via MilanNews.

According to recent reports, serie A seems to be struggling compared to other Italian sports. What could be done to make football more competitive?

In a recent development, “You’re telling me about something we’re doing, Gerry Cardinale’s idea. He came to the world of Italian football after twenty-five years in sport.

“It’s about creating Milan Sport Entertainment, that is, creating other sports around Milan, combining other sports with football, providing entertainment, communicating, and using Milan and Milano – because he also places great importance on the city of Milan, which is one of Europe’s emerging cities – to create an attractive environment for other sports and other situations.

“I’ll give just one example: if you take the United States, which is a gigantic market for the world of sports, football comes in fifth among the sports that Americans love, after basketball, of course, and even after hockey.

Industry observers note that “So, how do we make football – and, in our case, Serie A – attractive in the United States? Precisely by creating this concept of entertainment around football, this concept of Milan, of fashion, of spectacle, that is, creating an attractiveness that competes with the other sports we compete with every day.

“This is the idea that Gerry brought in Italy, coming from his vast experience in the world of sport, and therefore around this we look to our future. Gerry Cardinale comes to say that he will never sell Milan, precisely because his project is a long-term one.”.

The Generali Stadium will be something more than a stadium and will help this….

Sources indicate that “Let’s say it’s been quite a complex journey. A very long one that I’ve been on with Inter since 2018-2019. But we’ve reached, let’s say, some key milestones. The first was in November last year, when we bought the San Siro stadium.

Industry observers note that “The Meazza belongs to Inter and Milan, and the entire surrounding area. So every now and then I read debates: ‘But should it be torn down, shouldn’t it be torn down?’. Well, this will be a decision we’ll make because it’s ours, so I want to say: we have a clear, notarial fact behind us that gives us ownership of the San Siro stadium.

“This was the first step. The second was the presentation of the stadium that we held a few weeks ago. I think the Milanese and the professionals liked this presentation of this stadium designed by two great architects: one who worked on the exterior of the stadium and another who was responsible for the division of the spaces inside.

Industry observers note that “Building a great stadium like this is something extremely key. Technical. Because then, as always when you tackle new topics, you learn things. I, for example, learned that Manica – this company that designs our stadium – has built six hundred stadiums around the world.

It has been revealed that “So, to say that building a stadium is a profession, it’s not something you improvise. And this was the second step. The third was that Generali seized the opportunity to own this fresh stadium and the old one as well, because the collaboration on the Generali Stadium begins now.

“They seized the opportunity to have the two great Milanese clubs in Milan, both of which have a history of victories, are known worldwide and have millions of fans worldwide, and to use this newly introduced stadium to promote their image, I would say especially in Europe – because Generali are a very European company – but I would also say worldwide.

Industry observers note that “They seized a great opportunity because opportunities like this are just the ones you get. And so I must say the negotiations concluded very successfully.”.

“We have all the authorisations in front of us by September 2027. Therefore, in principle, we could begin construction of the fresh stadium between the end of 2027 and the beginning of 2028. So, let’s say, we’re pretty close to the home stretch.

Sources indicate that “Naturally, as always with these complications, there may be some discussion points. Furthermore, in Milan we’re heading towards an election campaign for a upcoming mayor, and a topic like the construction of a new stadium is one that can naturally excite politicians.

“Let’s say we’re confident because the entire process we’ve taken so far protects us from these potential disruptions, and we’re fiercely determined to move forward. With the fresh stadium, among other things, we’ll have €100 million in additional revenue.

“This €100 million in additional revenue is a fundamental ingredient for the success of AC Milan, Inter Milan, and Serie A around the world, because ultimately, €100 million – to have great players, to pay great players – is a fundamental ingredient for success.”.

Wolves among Championship clubs interested in 18-goal/assist winger – his contract expires in December

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (560 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that wolves are mounting their challenge for an immediate return to Premier League football and sit 3rd in the Championship table.
  • Sources indicate that according to Sky Sports, among the players on Wanderers’ radar is Liel Abada.
  • Abada may not reach the requirements for a work permit, so he could be signed on a free transfer before being loaned out to a top-five league in Europe so he can gain the points needed to play in England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that wolves are mounting their challenge for an immediate return to Premier League football and sit 3rd in the Championship table. Their talented squad are in impressive form, but Cesar Peixoto and co will have eyes on potential reinforcements ahead of the January transfer window.

Sources indicate that according to Sky Sports, among the players on Wanderers’ radar is Liel Abada. The 25-year-old winger sees his contract at Charlotte FC expire in December, and his impending free agent status means he is being tracked by a number of Championship clubs.

There is a catch, however. Abada may not reach the requirements for a work permit, so he could be signed on a free transfer before being loaned out to a top-five league in Europe so he can gain the points needed to play in England.

Abada may be a name some fans are familiar with. After starting out in his native Israel with Maccabi Petah Tikva, he moved to Celtic in the summer of 2021 and spent a little under three years with the Scottish club.

According to recent reports, he was a hit at Parkhead, managing 29 goals and 22 assists in 112 games. Abada has found success in the MLS with Charlotte FC too, with 11 goals and seven assists in the 2026 campaign taking him to 24 goals and 11 assists in 97 outings for the club.

According to recent reports, wolves target Abada can play on both wings as he is good with both feet. Without a doubt, his biggest asset is his speed and agility, as it makes him a threat when running at his man or getting the jump on the backline to run in behind. He is technically adept too though, allowing him to cut inside and link up with central players.

According to recent reports, abada has ended the 2026 season in fine goalscoring form as well. He scored a hat-trick off the bench in a 4-0 win over CF Montreal, and two games later, he scored twice in a 3-3 draw against Inter Miami.

After dropping from the Premier League, Wolves don’t really have a weak area in their squad. They have talented players on the wings too, so a deal for Abada isn’t a glaring need.

However, with Enso Gonzalez down the pecking order and Bertrand Traore’s impact limited by injury, a true specialist winger could help Wanderers in their bid to break into the Championship’s top two.

Abada would be strong competition for the likes of Rafiki Noted, Mateus Mane and Rodrigo Gomes. He can join for nothing and further strengthen Peixoto’s frontline, and at 25, he has the time and room to grow into a potential Premier League player for the Old Gold.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan have chosen the centre-forward they want in January, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport: Nicolo Tresoldi.
  • The newspaper write this morning that the ballot is settled, and there’s a winner: Milan have opted for Tresoldi as their attacking target in view of the winter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan have chosen the centre-forward they want in January, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport: Nicolo Tresoldi.

The newspaper write this morning that the ballot is settled, and there’s a winner: Milan have opted for Tresoldi as their attacking target in view of the winter. Part of the reason for this is because Endrick – the alternative name – made his intentions clear: “I hope to spend my life at Real Madrid.”.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In this story of preferences, Tresoldi’s choice is also crucial. The 22-year-old has supported Milan since he was a child, while in Belgium and beyond he has proven himself to be a goal scorer. Inter found this out, as he scored a hat-trick against them in the Champions League at San Siro.

According to recent reports, the No.9 shirt and role is right now occupied by Gonçalo Ramos, not a trivial thing due to the record-breaking fee paid for him last summer. However, Ruben Amorim genuinely believes the Portuguese can co-exist with Tresoldi, who can be on hand to finish the chances created by Ramos’ movement.

It has been revealed that tresoldi is a true ‘devil’ in the penalty area. He has 18 goals this season for club (eight in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Belgian Super Cup) and another four for Germany’s U21s. This leaves him just shy of 20 goals, in mid-November.

It has been revealed that tresoldi is also desperate to move to Milan and if it were up to him, the deal would be done. His desire to join his boyhood club could prove helpful and provide a boost to the deal’s success, just as it has before. His agents and family are equally positive about a potential Italian move.

Club Brugge are in a different mood, however, and would happily keep him unless offered at least €60m. Just a few months ago, the Belgian giants rejected offers just over half that. This is a figure Milan are willing to negotiate around, because Champions League qualification is crucial and goals are needed to achieve this.

Besides, Cardinale is of the opinion that it’s better to invest now than risk deepening the deficit. Another year without the revenues from the top club competition would be far from ideal for many different reasons.

What about Francesco Camarda? Here too, the debate is over: the club and the coach agree on the need for a loan, perhaps abroad. Camarda agrees: he knows he needs to regain rhythm by playing regularly, to help his development.

For Milan, it would be another negotiation with Brugge after Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari. The deal for the former was conducted by Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara, while for the latter it was Igli Tare. Now, Cardinale intends to do things himself.

It has been revealed that the owner wants Tresoldi and is ready to sit at the table himself, while Nicolò remains ready to serve him a winning first pass. Milan want him in January, but if that weren’t possible, they would leave the discussion open for the summer.

#61213. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5876 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • According to recent reports, we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

According to recent reports, we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most key positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the significant difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Industry observers note that zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, debuted a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

In a recent development, it was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

It has been revealed that suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

It has been revealed that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Recent findings suggest that asked if Tottenham had made a substantial mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi stated: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa upcoming boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

Recent findings suggest that “They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery mentioned. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

In a recent development, “Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

vs Man City (H) - Oct 24th, 12.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia shows his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

Sources indicate that “We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we demonstrated a really good character.”.

Recent findings suggest that and that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

In a recent development, late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

In a recent development, this will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Industry observers note that callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

In a recent development, though Savio takes the corner quickly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

Maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

It has been revealed that kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

But it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

In a recent development, A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

The Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

Villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

According to recent reports, gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

According to recent reports, marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his latest club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

He gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

According to recent reports, robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

So close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

In a recent development, huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

Ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

Tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being quickly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

Savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

But the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

Savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

We’re back in action in north London.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus.

Villa: Wan-Bissaka for Matty Cash.

Sources indicate that and as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

It looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

Possession: Spurs 57% vs 44% Villa.

Good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side currently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

In a recent development, tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

According to recent reports, there has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

In a recent development, but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bradford City are up for sale, but the price put on the club by owner Stefan Rupp could be off-putting to those seeking to buy into the West Yorkshire club.

Bradford City marked their return to League action following the international break with a 2-2 home draw against Doncaster Rovers. A Sean Grehan goal for Doncaster salvaged the visitors a point, but the draw was still enough to lift the Bantams back into the play-off places as a result of Plymouth Argyle's surprise 2-0 home defeat to Peterborough United.

But while Bradford's current position remains encouraging, there has been a degree of uncertainty surrounding the future of the club amid reports that owners Stefan Rupp and Edin Radic could be planning to sell up and move on.

The club are reportedly of interest to a Thai consortium who are looking to buy a club and who have had an interest in EFL clubs in the past.

Reporting on his Patreon on Sunday morning, journalist Alan Nixon has reported that the asking price for Bradford City is £11 million, though he adds that this price doesn't include the club's Valley Parade home itself, which has been owned by the pension fund of former chairman Gordon Gibb since 2004.

Nixon confirms that "there is interest in the Yorkshire club and they could potentially be sold", but adds that "the owners are looking for an eight-digit sum and that seems high when they do not own the ground".

Would you support newly introduced ownership at Bradford City, or would you rather stick with the current group? Let us know in the comments below!

However, he does add that this doesn't necessarily mean the end of interest in buying them, saying that, "potential buyers have been in contact with Gordon Gibb, the Valley Parade landlord, and could go in with him".

Although Gibb hasn't been directly involved in the running of Bradford City in over two decades, he is a key player in any sale of the club, despite being based in Scarborough and being a Leeds United fan - the Whites are West Yorkshire rivals of the Bantams, but of course they are two divisions apart.

It has been revealed that selling a club in the bottom two divisions of the EFL which doesn't own its own ground is very different to selling a club which does. Since the other assets that the club owns aren't usually especially valuable, the ground itself is often by far the biggest and most valuable that the club owns.

Industry observers note that those who buy a club which doesn't own its own home are usually buying little more than the contracts, the right to play in the EFL, and the name of the club itself. Many prospective owners will want to 'reunite' the club with its ground when they purchase it, as happened with Coventry City last year, where owner Doug King managed to secure the purchase of The CBS Arena, almost three years after buying the club itself.

Sources indicate that bradford reportedly pay more than £500,000 annually to lease the ground, with the existing agreement due for renewal in 2028, and that amount of money as an ongoing cost limits what the club can spend elsewhere. But Gibb is under no obligation to sell, and it's not known what he would want for it.

The last set of company accounts for the club confirmed that a "net loss of (£996,814) in 2024 has been augmented by a further loss in the current year of (£2,992,958)", so Bradford City are not currently profitable, and any latest owners would be aware that profitability might only come should they manage to get the club all the way up to the Premier League.

Industry observers note that but Bradford City have been moving in an upward direction over the last two or three years following years of stagnation in League Two, and the size of the club, who can still attract attendances of close to 20,000 and represent a city of half a million people, will be appealing to investors looking for a project that they can grow. But the cost of the stadium itself is a clear complication in the sale of the club, and it might mean that negotiations take some time to conclude.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stoke City have leapfrogged Birmingham City in the Championship table after a narrow 1-0 victory over the Blues at the bet365 Stadium on Saturday, as Potters wing-back Luca Bombino sends a message to the home supporters.

Stoke have climbed to 2nd in the Championship table after beating Birmingham at the weekend, remaining level on points with Middlesbrough, but with a slightly worse goal difference than the Teesside outfit.

The Potters, following their victory over Blues, have become the first club in the division to win ten league games this season, as one player has sent a message to supporters after his day ended early.

George Hirst's goal just after half-time would prove to be the decisive one, as the Scottish forward netted just his second goal for Stoke following his potential £10 million move from Ipswich Town over the summer.

With the home side in control and looking for a second, American wing-back Luca Bombino mistimed his challenge on Patrick Roberts whilst already on a yellow card, as referee Robert Madley had no choice but to give the 20-year-old his marching orders just past the hour mark.

Stoke withstood everything Birmingham could throw at them, and Bombino's red card ultimately didn't affect the result, as the American has taken to social media to share a message with supporters.

In his post, the 20-year-old apologised for his mistake, made known how proud he is of his teammates' performance despite his blunder, and thanked the Stoke fans for their support.

His red card means he will miss his side's Championship home clash with Millwall on Wednesday evening, where either Eric Bocat or Justin Devenny will presumably take his role at left wing-back, as Stoke supporters have shared their thoughts over Bombino's red.

After three defeats to open the campaign, Stoke have responded with an incredible ten wins in their next 13 league games and are flying.

Bombino's red card was the only damp spot on a bright day for the Potters on Saturday, as Stoke fans have taken to social media to react to the American's sending-off.

Stoke fans are no different to many other sets of supporters, in that they love a tackle, and they adore 110 per cent effort, as Bombino epitomises that.

The only thing the American can do now is learn from this situation and ensure similar mistakes don't happen moving forward.

Stoke supporters will always forgive a player as long as they give it their all and show passion, and in Bombino's case, he has likely already been forgiven by the masses.

This Potters fan backs the 20-year-old to get just fine at the club.

Either Bocat or Devenny will take Bombino's place at left wing-back against Millwall midweek, as Bombino will have to fight his way back into the side upon his return.

Bombino had only played for San Diego in the MLS before his move to North Staffordshire in the summer, and whilst his rawness prevailed in this game, there is belief he will come good in due course.

Recent findings suggest that what do you make of Bombino's red card? Can Stoke continue to sustain this level of form moving forward? How do you see the Potters faring from here on out? Share your thoughts below.

With his side claiming a huge three points against promotion rivals Birmingham, Stoke manager Mark Robins will have no intention of slowing down anytime soon.

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 05:36 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:52 EST, 19 November 2026.

A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

It has been revealed that one is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career. The other is a 34-year-old Argentinian who won the 2022 World Cup and has appeared 234 times in the Premier League.

We mention those brief backgrounds because when assessing who will give him the greater chance of stopping Leeds United from scoring on Saturday, Xabi Alonso takes them into account. Indeed, Alonso told us so while covering Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

One conversation with the manager was centred on his goalkeeper options. At that time, they were Penders and Robert Sanchez.

Industry observers note that alonso praised Penders’ potential but explained to us how highly he values ‘experience’ in his goalkeeper. ‘To have this security in goal is important,’ he insisted when asked.

According to recent reports, sanchez was indeed nominated as his No 1 for their first fixture of the Premier League season at Fulham. The 29-year-old Spaniard had a stinker, which led to him being loaned to Como. It is a straightforward loan, and he has been second-choice to Jean Butez under Cesc Fabregas, so there is a chance he will be back at Chelsea next summer, but that is a problem for another day.

A Daily Mail Sport poll of almost 2,000 Chelsea fans resulted in 57.9 per cent voting in favour of Mike Penders (above) keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

Martinez is available for the first time since breaking his jaw at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Martinez arrived from Aston Villa for £7.5million, was told he would be Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper, and is now available again. He is able to play without a protective mask, as he did while representing Argentina in their 7-0 friendly win over Costa Rica on Tuesday night.

It was his first appearance since breaking his jaw at Everton and having surgery exactly a month prior. He headed back to London after that victory to return to Chelsea, presumably under the impression that he will be playing against Leeds come Saturday.

It has been revealed that it is Alonso who will have the ultimate say on who goes in goal, in conjunction with his head of goalkeeping, Ben Roberts, and assistant goalkeeping coach, James Russell. That decision will be communicated with his chosen goalkeeper in the build-up, though Alonso is unlikely to tell us when we ask him at his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

One insider consulted this week stated his suspicion is the Argentinian will make an immediate return because it would create a headache for Alonso. Martinez is a massive character, volatile, and, if reduced to second choice, would not be pleased.

Statistically, Leeds cross the ball more than most in the Premier League, which could be more challenging for Penders than Martinez.

Filling in for Martinez, Penders punched the ball into his own goal on his first league start for Chelsea in a 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur.

However, he impressed against Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, then Manchester United and Sunderland in the Premier League. He won the Save of the Month award for October for denying Bryan Mbeumo at Stamford Bridge.

Penders won October's Save of the Month award for denying Man United's Bryan Mbeumo.

Penders is clearly a terrific talent, and it would be tempting to continue to show trust in him by having him face Leeds. Chelsea then face Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace, Liverpool and Manchester City in a rush of fixtures as we head into December.

It is a major decision to be made by Alonso, and would take bravery for him to stick with his prodigy in Penders, when we know the experience of the proven Martinez weighs heavy in his mind.

Chelsea vice captain Moises Caicedo is to be checked over at Cobham after a small injury scare while the influential midfielder was away with Ecuador.

Caicedo would be expected to wear the armband at Leeds in Reece James’ ongoing absence. He is set to return to the training ground on Thursday to be assessed.

The 25-year-old played 84 minutes in Ecuador’s first fixture of the break, a 2-0 victory against Costa Rica in which he scored. However, he then asked to be substituted at half-time of their 2-0 win over Bolivia, which ended in the early hours of Wednesday morning. Captaining his country, it was believed to be due to a small physical complaint.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Chelsea have been looking at the midfield market in the build-up to this January after they missed out on bolstering their options in the summer when Enzo Fernandez was sold to Manchester City. They retain an interest in Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

QPR have had a brilliant start to the season, and the prospect of finishing in a play-off spot for the first time since their relegation to the Championship way back in 2015 seems a lot more attainable as the year goes on.

Julien Stephan's side right now occupy the final position in the revamped play-offs and are playing some of the best football in the second tier, per the underlying numbers. They have the fourth-best xG difference in the league, and only Middlesbrough and Wolves have a better xGA.

A lot of the players who QPR signed in the past few seasons, either from League One or as youngsters from Premier League clubs and abroad, are starting to blossom into very good top-end Championship players, and it's being reflected in their results.

In a recent development, there's apt depth everywhere in the squad, perhaps other than in central midfield. Ball-playing centre-back Ronnie Edwards, who has played in the engine room before at Peterborough United, has been called in to deputise at times, either due to Nicolas Madsen's injury or a lack of form for Jonathan Varane.

Glen Kamara was QPR's marquee midfield signing this past summer, with the former play-off finalist at Leeds United joining on loan to form an engine room core with Madsen and Varane.

Sources indicate that however, the Hoops' unlucky history with injuries in recent times caught up with Madsen, who should be back shortly. But it did leave Julien Stephan light in those areas and, as mentioned, Edwards was called in to deputise as Kamara worked his way into the side, coming in instead of Varane.

Therefore, FLW's QPR fan pundit, Louis Moir, wants to see his side bolster their midfield options in case injury strikes again, and would like to see Fulham's Harrison Reed arrive on loan.

Recent findings suggest that "One player I'd like to see join, and I'm not sure it's even that ambitious, is Harrison Reed. I've always liked him as a player across the years; he's really tidy, neat, does the hard work and has shown his ability in the Premier League," he stated.

"I think with this season, Madsen has been out a bit, Kamara has obviously come in and has been class, but Varane hasn't been at his best, so we're kind of lacking in midfield.

According to recent reports, "You never want a serious injury to occur to someone like Kamara, for example, and Edwards has come in and done a great job in midfield, but I just feel we could do with one more, and that's mainly due to Varane not being at his best. I think it [the midfield] can be a weak point if Madsen or Kamara are out.".

Sources indicate that varane was one of QPR's best performers pre-Stephan, to the point where the Hoops were reportedly rejecting £4 million offers from La Liga side Espanyol for his services. There is a player there, but that hasn't been seen this season, especially. With Reed in the squad, the R's could maintain this early-season play-off form if injuries do continue to haunt them.

Reed is well-respected at Fulham and has been a great servant to the club in the seven years he's been playing at Craven Cottage. However, the club is starting to outgrow the 31-year-old.

Recent findings suggest that he made just seven league appearances last season, remaining unused from the bench on 22 separate occasions. Funnily enough, one of those cameo bench appearances saw him score the Premier League's Goal of the Season in a 2-2 draw with Liverpool in January.

Industry observers note that this season, under Alvaro Arbeloa, Reed's role in the squad has decreased even further. Now, the midfielder isn't getting into matchday squads in the Premier League, and all his appearances so far have been in the EFL Cup.

According to recent reports, do you think Harrison Reed will be a primary loan target for Championship sides this summer? Let us know in the comments.

"I think Reed may be of interest to a few Championship clubs," says Moir, due to his standing in the Fulham fold. "But him on loan would be more than ideal and a really top signing.

"I think it's more than realistic, more than ambitious, and would fit in really well. He'd add a lot of bite to the midfield and more depth. You wouldn't have to worry about him starting each week, but he'd come on and do a good job.".

According to recent reports, reed's long-term future at Fulham is up in the air. The 31-year-old's four-year deal, which he signed back in 2023, is up at the end of the campaign.

There is an option for the Cottagers to extend that by a year, but the likelihood of that happening seems quite slim, especially if Arbeloa's side remain in the Premier League this season.

So, Reed could be in a situation where a loan move in January could almost be a way for a loaning team to have a six-month trial before a decision is made about handing him a longer-term contract.

According to recent reports, if QPR remain a Championship side, this could definitely be a decision that they make. Reed has 131 Premier League appearances and has won promotion from the Championship twice with Fulham. At 32, he could be the perfect veteran option in the middle for a side that were on the cusp of promotion and want to go again in 2027/28.

Obviously, the Hoops will want to go up this year, and Reed could help aid in that, too, but thinking longer term, getting the 31-year-old through the door could be quite an underrated move for this R's side.

Christian Pulisic revealed his emotions after scoring a brilliant bicycle kick during the USA’s final game under Mauricio Pochettino.

It was known before the USMNT’s two-legged UEFA Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti that it would be Pochettino’s last two games, given that he has an agreement in place to take over the job at Manchester United vacated following Michael Carrick’s dismissal.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The stars and stripes certainly gave him a fitting send-off, as they won the first leg 6-0 a few days ago and then completed the job with a 2-0 victory in Cincinnati last night. Pulisic got the first goal after a brace in the previous rout, and it was an incredible overhead kick.

Industry observers note that pulisic was actually overlooked by Pochettino for the September-October window – partly for fitness reasons – and he spoke to reporters after the game to share his thoughts after an emotional evening. He was called the ‘best player on the pitch’ by the US media, and his words are via MilanNews.

An overhead kick goal is pretty special….

“I’ve never scored a goal like that, it was special. Weston crossed the ball and it was the only thing I could really do, so I thought I had to give it a try. It was really nice to see the ball go in.”.

Is it nice to get a victory on Pochettino’s farewell day?

“Yes, obviously he’s leaving now, so it’s nice to end with a good performance and a nice win for the team.”.

How would you describe this particular group, a mix of veterans and young players?

According to recent reports, “It’s really nice. It’s been fun working with everyone. We got to meet some of the newly introduced guys, even some young talent, and obviously there’s still some of the same core group, so it’s a really great team. I really like where we are right now and I think we’re still growing and have a great future ahead of us.”.

What does Pochettino’s last match leave you with?

“We’re in a good place. Overall, I think the team has improved. I think there’s a good culture within the group, and I think we should be really excited about the future.”.

What kind of an impact has Julian Hall made?

Sources indicate that “It was fantastic playing with him. He scored a goal, but also just for his overall play, making lots of runs and causing problems for the other team. He did a great job, fitting in with this team and making his mark.”.

What was Mauricio Pochettino’s farewell message to you this evening?

Sources indicate that “Simply that we have a truly extraordinary culture. We’ve built something truly special and that a bright future awaits us. And to continue that by letting the rest of the team support us.”.

Does it really matter who the coach is at this point?

“I mean, not that it doesn’t matter. Ultimately, it’s not our choice, as players. We hope whoever arrives will be able to capitalise on the things we do so well and lead us in the right direction.”.

  • The Rams sit 23rd in the table after 16 games with just 10 points to their name, and their misery was compounded after returning from the international break with a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Southampton on Saturday.
  • There was a sense of optimism around Pride Park ahead of the start of the new season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derby County have been one of the surprise packages in the Championship so far this season, but for all the wrong reasons.

The Rams sit 23rd in the table after 16 games with just 10 points to their name, and their misery was compounded after returning from the international break with a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Southampton on Saturday.

There was a sense of optimism around Pride Park ahead of the start of the new season. After last term's excellent eighth place finish and the expansion of the play-offs, there was a real sense that Derby could finally have a crack at promotion to the Premier League.

John Eustace had worked wonders since his arrival in February 2025, building a squad that was seemingly capable of fighting at the sharp end of the Championship.

However, with just one win in 14 league matches to start the upcoming season, the Rams were left cut adrift with Burnley and Preston in the relegation zone, with no escape looking likely.

A much-needed victory over Bolton Wanderers in the final game before the early November international break gave supporters hope that things could turn around, but Saturday's defeat at St Mary's was a depressing thud back down to reality.

Following Saturday's defeat at Southampton, Rams defender Dion Sanderson faced BBC Sport Derby to give his verdict on a difficult run of fixtures ahead, and it's fair to say his words will cut deep for supporters.

"Everything's different, different teams, we prepare differently each week," Sanderson noted.

"But I think from a personal note, it doesn't matter what team you're up against, you've got to play for the badge on your shirt, play for the club, and play for yourself, a bit of pride.

"I think the lads this week, especially, have got to continue [the intensity in training]. We've got to take that onto next week and the week after.

"We are in a relegation scrap and that's the reality of it. The lads need to start pulling their socks up now, and we're asking a lot from everyone," the defender concluded.

After just 16 games, a player admitting that a relegation scrap is on the cards certainly isn't what fans will want to be hearing, especially after how much optimism there was heading into the season.

After the interview with Sanderson was posted to X by BBC Sport Derby, some Rams supporters reacted to what their centre-back had to say in the wake of yet another disappointing defeat.

One fan remained surprisingly positive, suggesting Derby did enough to earn a point and encouraged the players to keep their heads up.

Another wasn't quite as forgiving, calling Sanderson 'hopeless'.

Another also voiced their frustrations at Sanderson himself, suggesting he should let his performances do the talking rather than post-match interviews.

Finally, one fan blamed club CEO Stephen Pearce for the mess the club at the moment finds itself in, and suggested nothing will get better until he is replaced.

5 managers Watford FC must eye up ASAP after Dionisi sack ft ex-Arsenal coach

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1232 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Continuing to struggle down at the bottom end of the Championship table, Watford have now taken the decision to sack manager Alessio Dionisi.
  • Following a 5-1 defeat to Cardiff City last month, it was reported then that Dionisi was set to be sacked by Watford, but he held on and dismissed those reports.
  • There had been a slight improvement before the November international break, with the Hornets edging past Lincoln City before earning a creditable goalless draw against Middlesbrough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Continuing to struggle down at the bottom end of the Championship table, Watford have now taken the decision to sack manager Alessio Dionisi.

Following a 5-1 defeat to Cardiff City last month, it was reported then that Dionisi was set to be sacked by Watford, but he held on and dismissed those reports.

There had been a slight improvement before the November international break, with the Hornets edging past Lincoln City before earning a creditable goalless draw against Middlesbrough.

However, they have returned from the break with a 4-0 shellacking at the hands of Sheffield United at Bramall Lane and that has prompted Dionisi to be let go of by The Hornets.

As a result, we have taken a look at five potential candidates to replace the former Empoli manager in Hertfordshire as Watford fight to keep their second-tier status.

Former Ecuador boss Sebastian Beccacece remains unemployed since leading the South Americans to the round of 32 of FIFA World Cup 2026, eventually losing to Mexico at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

It had been a frustrating time in the group stages for the Ecuadoreans; unfortunately beaten 1-0 by Cote d’Ivoire in their opener before being held to a shock goalless draw by Curaçao. They did then manage to squeeze through with a dramatic victory over Germany at the MetLife Stadium in New York.

Unable to score due to a lack of quality was an issue that plagued them throughout qualification, but a manager’s job is to get a team to create chances in attack and look organised at the back – two things Beccacece managed to do and impressively so in charge of Ecuador as they finished second in CONMEBOL qualification for the tournament, with just five goals conceded in their 18 qualifiers.

A lack of quality in the final third undermined the actual style of football that he had implemented and created with La Tri. He remains a highly-rated coach, and it would be an ambitious appointment for Watford to make but one that may be slightly more realistic after a frustrating summer for the Argentine.

Earlier this season, Parma parted company with manager Carlos Cuesta after a slow-ish start to the campaign. They have continued to struggle, though, and the lack of improvement, as shown by a 5-1 loss at home to Roma this weekend, only further speaks to the managerial qualities of Cuesta.

Recent findings suggest that cuesta, born in Majorca, began his professional coaching career as an assistant at Arsenal to Mikel Arteta from 2020 until the summer of 2025. He was poached by expected Serie A strugglers Parma at the age of just 29, turning 30 later in the month after his appointment.

In his debut season as a manager, and such a young one at that, Parma comfortably survived with an extremely impressive defensive record, perhaps to be expected by a duel-led, conservative-focused apprentice of Arteta.

Undermined by big-money defensive sales this summer, such as goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to Aston Villa and centre-back Alessandro Circati to Benfica, Parma were hasty in their decision to move on, fitting of being a Serie A club but a decision that they are perhaps already regretting and could open the door for Watford to find a real coup.

Without much of a playing career to discuss, Edward Iordanescu began his coaching as an assistant, and occasional caretaker, coach at Steaua Bucharest before going on to experience a bit of a journeyman career across Romania.

Iordanescu coached Fortuna Brazi and Targu Mures in 2013 before a couple of years in charge of Pandurii Targu Jiu and then short stints at CSKA Sofia, Astra Giurgiu, CFR Cluj and Gaz Metan Medias before returning to CFR Cluj for the 2020-21 campaign.

Having won the league title as well as a couple of Supercupa Romaniei with CFR Cluj, Iordanescu returned to FCSB, the artist formerly known as Steaua, before getting the Romania job in 2022. In charge of the national team, he led them to UEFA EURO 2024 qualification and even into the knockout stages of that competition before they were beaten 3-0 by the Netherlands in Munich.

His most recent job saw him take charge of Polish giants Legia Warsaw, but he was sacked in October of the same 2025-26 season after an average start to the campaign.

He was heavily linked with the job a few weeks ago and has held talks with the hierarchy, and so his name cropping again would be no surprise, despite his nomadic managerial career.

At the age of 65, it would certainly be a punt for Watford to give Jose Luis Mendilibar his first job in English football, but it would be a real coup for The Hornets should they choose to do so.

Old school in terms of his football values and general tactical philosophy, stereotypically Basque in that respect, Mendilibar has repeatedly got his teams to punch above their weight; be it taking Eibar into La Liga and making them a top-flight stalwart or leading Real Valladolid to a record points tally in the second-tier while reaching the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey or performing a ‘great escape’ from La Liga relegation with Osasuna.

He was the firefighter brought in to keep fallen giants Sevilla from falling down to the second-tier after a poor stint in charge from Jorge Sampaoli; keeping the Andalusians up and also managing to win the UEFA Europa League, too.

Industry observers note that he then took charge of Olympiacos and added a second European trophy to his cabinet with the Greek giants defeating Aston Villa in the semi-finals and Fiorentina in the final to win the UEFA Europa Conference League. Not able to sustain their best over a season eventually led to his dismissal, but title-challenging consistency is not required at Watford; grit, aggression and intensity it and Mendilibar provides that in abundance.

A slightly different style, but again, looking to Spain for an appointment could see Watford try and poach Almeria boss Garcia Pimienta.

Once one of the more highly-regarded young coaches in Spain, after beginning his coaching career at Barcelona B, Garcia Pimienta led Las Palmas to La Liga playing in a stereotypically Canarian manner, with Las Palmas often referred to as ‘the Brazilians of Spanish football’ and their passing style of football on their ascent was representative of that.

He was eventually poached from Las Palmas by Spanish giants Sevilla, but he was just one of many victims of Sevilla’s decline both on and off the pitch in recent years before rebuilding his reputation across Andalusia and at Almeria.

Pimienta took charge of an Almeria side that had lost the play-off final to regional rivals Malaga in the summer and have substantial expectations to get back into La Liga and to kick on further than that with their spending.

Who should Watford appoint as their new manager? Comment below!

So far this season, they have managed to collect 32 points from 14 matches, sitting five points clear of third place Granada but just a point behind league leaders Castellon, with Pimienta again showing his class and potential outside of the basket case of Seville, where even that now in hindsight looks like a reasonable job.

Once linked with Watford in 2025, could Pimienta now head to Vicarage Road? It wouldn't be a surprise if he was on Gino Pozzo's radar.

Upcoming footage shows what Ryan Manning did during Southampton's 2nd goal v Derby County

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Southampton strolled to a comfortable 2-0 victory over Derby County at the weekend, but what Ryan Manning did in the build-up to the second goal ought to have Saints fans laughing.
  • Southampton have continued to climb the Championship table with their latest 2-0 home victory over struggling Derby at St Mary's on Saturday, courtesy of goals from Cyle Larin and Divin Mubama.
  • Despite Derby's insistence on disrupting Southampton's flow, the home side dominated large parts of the game and were deserving of the three points in the end, as Irish left-back Manning has certainly had the last laugh.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton strolled to a comfortable 2-0 victory over Derby County at the weekend, but what Ryan Manning did in the build-up to the second goal ought to have Saints fans laughing.

Southampton have continued to climb the Championship table with their latest 2-0 home victory over struggling Derby at St Mary's on Saturday, courtesy of goals from Cyle Larin and Divin Mubama.

Despite Derby's insistence on disrupting Southampton's flow, the home side dominated large parts of the game and were deserving of the three points in the end, as Irish left-back Manning has certainly had the last laugh.

It took Southampton a while to really get going in their clash against Derby, with just one shot on target from either side in the first half, making it an extremely close encounter.

However, Eckert's half-time team talk appeared to have the effect the German would've been hoping for, as the Saints broke the deadlock with Larin just before the hour mark, before finally adding a second in the dying embers as Mubama raced through on goal to prod into an empty net following a Derby corner.

With Rams goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterström trying his luck in the penalty area in the closing stages, Mubama broke away after Lewis Dobbin played him through on goal, and running alongside the Manchester City loanee was Manning, who turned and appeared to laugh at the chasing Derby defenders.

The 30-year-old, who has developed into one of the best left-backs on the South Coast, has certainly endeared himself to the Southampton supporters since his arrival at the club in 2023, with this just being a fresh reminder of his character and importance to the side.

Manning's contract at St Mary's is due to expire in the summer, and as things stand, he's set to leave as a free agent in 2027.

However, he has made his intentions of staying at the club abundantly clear already, and having become a mainstay under Eckert, it would be a surprise if he wasn't offered fresh terms on the South Coast, regardless of whether a return to the Premier League is secured.

The Irishman will be free to speak to other clubs over a summer move in January, and with just over a month until the winter window, Southampton shouldn't leave this problem unresolved for much longer.

What have you made of Ryan Manning's time at Southampton? Would you like to see him offered a fresh deal? Share your thoughts below!

With Southampton climbing into the Championship play-off picture, Eckert will have set his sights firmly on the automatic promotion places right now.

If it weren't for their four-point deduction at the beginning of the campaign, the Saints would currently sit in 3rd place behind only Middlesbrough and Stoke City, level on points with Wolverhampton Wanderers but with a superior goal difference.

A return to the Premier League is certainly on the agenda in Hampshire, and Eckert will be looking to the likes of Manning to steer his side in the right direction over the course of the campaign.

Latest Update: Why Emile Heskey decided Bolton Wanderers would be his final club

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Premier League, Championship and England international forward, Emile Heskey, has revealed exactly why he opted to retire after a spell with Bolton Wanderers in the mid-2010s.

The 48-year-old turned out for some of English football's most historic clubs during a 22-year career, which included a high-profile switch from boyhood club, Leicester City, to Liverpool for £11m in the year 2000.

Heskey accumulated 62 England caps and netted seven goals during his esteemed career, as well as winning eight major honours.

Having racked up 516 appearances in the Premier League alongside 110 goals and 49 assists, Heskey then returned to Championship level for the first time in 18 years in December 2014 when he initially signed a short-term contract at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

After leaving Liverpool in 2004, Heskey went on to feature for Birmingham City, Wigan Athletic and Aston Villa, as well as a two-season spell with Newcastle Jets of the Australian A-League between 2012 and 2014.

Returning to England in late 2014, it was confirmed the striker would sign an initial short-term contract with the Whites, who were managed by Heskey's former Leicester teammate, Neil Lennon, at the time.

During his final career stint, he was partnered with Icelandic striker, Eidur Gudjohnsen, who had returned to the North West for a second spell earlier in December 2014, with the latter providing a debut goal for Heskey against Blackburn Rovers on Boxing Day of 2014.

In total, Heskey made 48 appearances for Wanderers, but his only full season at the club and the last of his career ended in relegation to League One, before he became one of 13 players who departed upon the expiration of their contracts.

Heskey started just 15 Championship games in his final career season, scoring twice against Charlton Athletic and Brighton and Hove Albion, but had already surpassed his 38th birthday at the midpoint of the campaign.

There are several examples of one-time top-level strikers continuing to lead the line into their 40s, but speaking to current Burnley forward, Jamie Vardy, Heskey revealed how he knew it was time for him to call it quits on his playing days.

"I went to Australia for two years then came back to Bolton," he stated.

"It was basically, in training, more or less, when you see young kids running past you, and you think, not 'I can't do this anymore', because I could've, and I was in good shape and I felt fine, but I didn't want people running past me and not being able to tackle and get back at them like my head was telling me I could do.

"I was like, 'Do I really want to keep going down the leagues to League One and League Two and continue there', just for what?," Heskey admitted.

Bolton fans, did Emile Heskey still impress you in his career's latter stages? Comment below!

"My boys were getting bigger, and I just decided that was enough for me. I got to 38 and probably could've played another one or two years, I think.".

Vardy, 39, is known for his remarkable 200-goal exploits at Leicester, during which he won the Premier League, FA Cup, Community Shield and two Championship titles between 2012 and 2025.

However, he then admitted to Heskey that he has had similar conversations with ex-professionals who may have retired earlier in their 30s, with the Sheffield native still turning out on a regular basis in the second tier.

There are shades between the final club stint of Heskey's career and his own, with Burnley right now in a dire predicament in the Championship after relegation from the Premier League, as they could emulate the unwanted feats of Luton Town and Leicester and become the third team to suffer successive relegations from the top-flight to League One in as many years.

Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails.
  • As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points.
  • When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

According to recent reports, it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

According to recent reports, any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

It has been revealed that don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

In a recent development, “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

Sources indicate that one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

Sources indicate that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose stated. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

In a recent development, speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

In a recent development, jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that showed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

Sources indicate that cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young mentioned on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose massive players and you get the opportunities. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.
