📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.
  • With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.
  • United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

According to recent reports, andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Recent findings suggest that fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

It has been revealed that with a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Industry observers note that juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

In a recent development, liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Recent findings suggest that which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

According to recent reports, this allowed him to put his struggles behind him for a couple of weeks, but things are now getting tough with the Seleção as well. Last Saturday – in a 4-1 defeat against Denmark – he finished the match without even touching the ball in the penalty box.

It was frighteningly similar to the isolation seen at Milan, and the problem is that his numbers didn’t improve even in Wales. Portugal won 3-2 but not only did the former PSG man not get his name on the scoresheet, he also didn’t participate in any of the goals directly.

Sources indicate that his numbers in the 59 minutes he was on the pitch: 1 shot attempted (a header from Neto’s pass from the left in the 47th minute), 4/7 successful passes, 11 touches, and 1 unsuccessful dribble. The story of a striker who is not involved.

In a recent development, that’s not all, either. Gonçalo also angered Bruno Fernandes. It happened during a counter-attack, with the Portuguese captain breaking down the left and crossing low, expecting Ramos to be there. Gonçalo had stopped though, and Fernandes’s reprimand was inevitable.

The two would later have another exchange at the end of the match, with Bruno reminding his team-mate – who was disappointed to be brought off after less than an hour – of the responsibility of replacing a giant like Cristian Ronaldo. Oh, and Bruno Fernandes has been linked today, by the way.

In short, Goncalo Ramos is ‘twisted in a spiral he can’t seem to escape’. After the game in Cardiff last night, he has reached 661 minutes without a goal for club and country. The last one was exactly a month ago, on October 18th against Atalanta.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

In a recent development, scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his upcoming role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Carlo Pellegatti has painted a positive picture regarding AC Milan’s developments, one that puts last season’s collapse into perspective.

Rewinding to the end of May, it felt like Milan’s entire world have caved in. A 2-1 defeat at home to Cagliari – a game that they led in early on – in the final round of the season condemned the Rossoneri to a fifth-placed finish, meaning they missed out on Champions League football again.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This is after Massimiliano Allegri had the team in a title fight going into the Spring, but ultimately the decline was near-vertical towards the end of the campaign. He paid the price for this, as did the CEO Giorgio Furlani, sporting director Igli Tare and chief scout Geoffrey Moncada.

It has been revealed that in his latest column for MilanNews, Carlo Pellegatti has put forward the notion that the defeat to the Sardinians might turn out to be a blessing. Why? Because the reset that followed on a sporting and managerial level seems to already be taking a positive shape.

“Krosche and delight! It’s a somewhat obvious joke, but it captures the expectations of AC Milan fans. When will he arrive? November 27th, as I’ve been told, or in the first ten days of December, or even – I really hope not – January 1st?” he began.

“The difference in dates for the announcement of his upcoming role is by no means insignificant, because the January transfer window becomes a crucial turning point for Milan’s fortunes, both today and in the future.

“The sooner the Head of Football sits down at Casa Milan, the better he can weave his web to strengthen the team in the winter transfer window. This should have been the job of a year ago, but was not accomplished by a shortsighted management team that never understood the difference between costs and investments.

“It’s also a shame that Igli Tare is a person who respects roles and is attentive to internal balances. He had to, and this is his great regret, bypass those who managed Milan, to speak with Gerry Cardinale and explain the importance of the arrival of a striker and a defender, who would have allowed them to be in the Champions League today.

“I’m using a very bold paradox, one I’ve never admitted. If failing to qualify for the Champions League was the reason that pushed Gerry Cardinale to fire the key figures of the three worst and most disastrous years in Milan’s history, then, given the exciting future prospects, it would have been better to lose against Cagliari, which avoided prolonging the agony of our dear old AC Milan. A painful sacrifice that, I hope, will be repaid with success in the years to come.

“With a Cardinale who was too absent and distant, guilty, by his own admission, of having delegated the management of his club to unsuitable people, but who now becomes the protagonist of this newly introduced way of operating, reminiscent of the good old days.

“I obviously feel sorry for Tare and Allegri, who, despite having their responsibilities, were victims of a confusing, chaotic, and divisive situation, and through no fault of their own.

Sources indicate that “Returning to Krosche, I hope he promptly finds his feet in this Milan adventure that awaits him. I continue to believe that a highly experienced and highly skilled Italian operative, to work alongside the German director, could and can be of help to him and Milan, given the obvious difficulties of integrating into a world that is completely different from the German one.

Recent findings suggest that “Gerry Cardinale and his chief assistant, Massimo Calvelli, are convinced of the wisdom of their choice, after meeting several times with Markus Krosche. I think it’s crucial that he’s not only a skilled market operator, but also a valid on-field contact for Ruben Amorim.

“The Portuguese will then be able to discuss potential choices and decisions with his Head of Football. In short, it was a position in the organisational chart that was culpably neglected, with the results that were seen, until Gerry Cardinale himself imposed Igli Tare, who, in any case, did not have an easy job.

“I mentioned Massimo Calvelli, who, in the media, always appears to be somewhat out of the spotlight. Certainly not in operational terms, because, from what I know, he was the absolute protagonist and architect of transactions that brought approximately €825m into Milan’s coffers.

“He was certainly a skilled architect of the return of Adidas as a shirt sponsor, but also a key figure in the acquisition of Generali, which will give its name to the newly introduced stadium, this time with the collaboration, it is noted, of Paolo Scaroni.

“Therefore, he is a valuable executive who works behind the scenes, but with excellent results in terms of economic and financial aspects and also for the club’s image.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.

The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.

It has been revealed that thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad. However, this raises questions as to why some England supporters have turned on the defender after he has continued to perform well for Arsenal.

The answer lies with the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

White left the England World Cup camp in November 2022, returning home due to personal reasons. The FA confirmed that White will not return to the squad and asked that his privacy be respected.

He did not play in the first two group games for England and missed the last group game against Wales due to illness.

There were reports that White had fallen out with assistant manager Steve Holland, but neither the FA nor England management confirmed this was the reason he left.

Gareth Southgate later stated there were no problems between White and Holland and that White had simply withdrawn himself from selection after the tournament.

Industry observers note that this meant that White would never play for England again while Southgate was still manager. Some fans were clearly upset by this, as they felt White was shunning his country.

It has been revealed that when White returned under Tuchel in March 2026, he was met with a negative reaction. He was booed by the crowd when he scored his first-ever international goal against Uruguay. White was also booed in the same fashion against Japan.

According to recent reports, he has since explained that supporters might view the situation differently if they knew the full story. However, he has chosen not to reveal the private details behind his departure.

Tuchel has shown little concern about White being affected by the controversy.

The England boss mentioned after the win on Thursday that he had not heard any boos and praised White’s qualities, work ethic and desire to play for his country.

He believes White can help England win games and added that he has the backing of the coaching staff.

Arsenal fans will be unsurprised to learn that White is still a valuable asset for Mikel Arteta, offering defensive consistency and being able to play as a right or centre-back.

In a recent development, the bad press that White is receiving from England fans will not go away any time soon. However, he has not done anything to hurt his reputation at club level. The reasons why he left for the World Cup are personal.

Industry observers note that the main focus for Arsenal will be getting him match fit again. As for the England fans, we shall see.

Pat Nevin sees a lot of Newcastle United.

The former Chelsea and Everton winger a regular visitor at St James’ Park.

Pat Nevin often on media duties at United matches.

As a result of that, he has far more of a clue than your average pundit about Newcastle United, the good an the bad.

The one-time player was once again on media duties at St James’ Park on Saturday night for the Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match.

As is usually a case, his reaction to what he witnessed was pretty spot on.

It has been revealed that pat Nevin on BBC Radio Five Live, commenting on the first half moment when Bruno Guimaraes almost headed Arsenal into the lead: “That would have broken a few hearts around here, a great run from Bruno Guimaraes. A very deep header, he’s a deep-lying midfielder. These Newcastle fans have watched him so many times in black and white and that was a decent half-chance.”.

Pat Nevin after Eze gave Arsenal a 33rd minute lead: “You felt as though it was coming. The Newcastle midfielders pushed up further and the second they did so, they were shredded. That pass from Kai Havertz is an absolute delight, he’s such a special player. Eberechi Eze lashed it past goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.”.

Pat Nevin commenting after Harvey Barnes equalised four minutes after the break: “Newcastle have been fabulous at the start of the second half. They’ve closed down higher up the field, not giving Arsenal any time on the ball. They’ve struggled to be able to zip the ball about like they did in the first. But can Newcastle keep this up?”.

Malick Thiaw giving United a 2-1 lead, Pat Nevin: “Beyond amazing. There is not a Newcastle fan in this ground who could see this coming. They have come out with such a brilliant attitude in the second half. Dan Burn at the back post with nobody on him. Malick Thiaw has the easiest tap-in in the world.”.

Industry observers note that pat Nevin as the match moves into the nine minutes of added time and the score 2-2, Noni Madueke having equalised on 78 minutes: “This has got the feeling of a cup tie. I love that Newcastle don’t want to settle just for a point against the champions. But I think they’re running out of players, Lewis Hall has sat down.”.

Pat Nevin with a perfect summing up after the final whistle: “Isn’t it a joy when you think you know what’s going on in football but you know nothing at half-time. In the first half Arsenal were all over Newcastle, there was not one area where Arsenal were not better. Then three changes at half time and Newcastle were superb in the second half and the fans will be wondering where that has been all season? A great performance coming back after being a goal down. They revealed the capabilities they’ve got.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal look to build on their recent win over Liverpool as they return to the Emirates Stadium but will face an impressive London City Lionesses side who are a potent attacking threat on their travels.

Renée Slegers’ team have struggled to convert their strong performances into points in the league this season. They have lost their last four WSL games at home, however, becoming the first team in WSL history to draw four successive games at home.

In a recent development, their bad run must come to an end. They have taken just three points from their first nine league games so far this season, scoring a miserable total of 10 goals. However, they look like they have more in the tank and will need to be much more clinical in front of the goal.

The day also marks Slegers’ 50th game in charge of the WSL. The Dutch manager has only lost six league games so far this season, with only Chelsea having a better record from teams that have been ever-present in the division.

Arsenal can’t take their opposition lightly after London City’s impressive recent form. They have won two and drawn once in their last three away league games, scoring 12 goals.

It has been revealed that eder Maestre’s side has become a potent attacking force. Daniëlle van de Donk has provided four assists this season, and Delphine Cascarino has scored three goals and provided two assists.

It was well-publicised ahead of the match that Yasir Al-Rumayyan would be at St James’ Park for the Newcastle United match against Arsenal.

An up and down season so far for United.

A chance for the Newcastle United Chairman to see for himself at close quarters how things are now looking.

Yasir Al-Rumayyan seeing a game of two halves.

Newcastle United struggling to get out of their own half in the opening 45 minutes as Arsenal dominated and led 1-0 at the break.

Matthias Jaissle making three substitutions at the break and a totally different Newcastle United on show, by far the better team that ‘won’ the second half 2-1.

By the final whistle, Newcastle United had certainaly deserved at least a point, possibly all three.

The brilliant second half comeback was achieved due to the following 13 Newcastle United players and these 13 can be separated as follows:.

Already at St James’ Park pre-Eddie Howe:.

Tino Livramento, Malick Thiaw, Dan Burn, Lewis Hall, Sven Botman, Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Yoane Wissa, Anthony Elanga, William Osula.

Ahead of summer 2026, Newcastle United Chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan took control of transfers from Eddie Howe and gave it to Ross Wilson.

Eddie Howe (and then Matthias Jaissle) still having some say but Ross Wilson the one dictating the overall transfer policy and holding the power.

This isn’t unusual, many clubs having a similar strategy of handing the Sporting Director control of transfer policy.

Ross Wilson the key man this summer in deciding to sell Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, as well as not renewing the contracts of Kieran Trippier and a number of other older players.

Altogether, approximately £260m/£270m was committed on new signings by Ross Wilson to rebuild the Newcastle United team and squad. Yasir Al-Rumayyan must have been wondering where they all were in that second half against Arsenal….

Amar Dedic – Subbed off after playing the first 45 minutes against Arsenal Sean Steur – Subbed off after playing the first 45 minutes against Arsenal Nico Gonzalez – An unused sub Matias Fernandez-Pardo – An unused sub Bazoumana Toure – Left out of the matchday squad Aladji Bamba – Left out of the matchday squad Ewen Jaouen – Injured Ousmane Diabate – On loan for the season at Turkish top tier club Gençlerbirliği.

It is still early days and we need a lot longer to judge properly when it comes to allowing Ross Wilson control of transfers in and out.

However, there are inherent weaknesses with a system whereby the Sporting Director and not the Manager/Head Coach has control of selecting which players are signed and which are sold/let go.

As things stand, Matthias Jaissle clearly overwhelmingly feels he has to rely at this moment in time on players who came in before Ross Wilson’s summer of 2026. Players who have been at the club for some time, less star players such as Gordon, Tonali, Trippier and Bruno who the Sporting Director wanted/agreed to move on this summer.

By the end of this season we should have a better idea about his signings.

Industry observers note that I certainly don’t think it is a total disaster, at least not longer-term. I think already I have seen enough of the likes of Hornicek, Steur and Dedic to believe that they are decent additions. I think Fernandez-Pardi will work out and I believe Nico Gonzalez will be okay. With the others they clearly need more time before we can judge them at all.

However, you don’t always get to tomorrow, if you can’t get through today….

For me it is very clear that Matthias Jaissle has walked into a situation where he has been left well short by Ross Wilson of a fully stocked and prepared squad to take on this 2026-27 season.

Recent findings suggest that A case of needing to battle through this campaign and then hopefully as a group the summer 2026 signings can grow and help Newcastle United evolve. In the meantime, it is the established old guard that Matthias Jaissle will clearly need to have the main focus on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:49 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 11:59 EST, 19 November 2026.

One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.

It was reported by Bloomberg last week that a German lender, Oldenburgische Landesbank (OL), had pulled out of a deal that would have let Brazilian top-flight side Palmeiras take a large upfront payment against instalments City are due to pay them for midfielder Allan Elias, signed this summer for £32million with £2m add-ons. That bank views City as a reputational and financial risk.

The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Apollo was in the final stages of negotiating the loan to City Football Group (CFG) in September, when the deal collapsed after the ruling that they artificially inflated their financial position to the tune of more than £900m over nine years.

It has been revealed that city owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan injected £100m into the club in the month after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Mansour, who has only been present at one City home game since Abu Dhabi bought the club in 2008, has made no public comment on the club’s conviction, which delivers huge reputational damage to his image-conscious country.

There are signs that football is preparing for a strong legal attack from Abu Dhabi if City lose their appeal. Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors in the event of sponsors Etihad and Etisalat suing them, it was also confirmed on Thursday. Legal indemnity will be in place for CEO Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and three other non-executive directors.

US private capital group Apollo Global Management abandoned a £1.5billion loan to Man City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

City owner Sheikh Mansou injected £100m into the club after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi.

But the refusal of credit by Apollo, which has loaned £80m to Premier League football club Nottingham Forest and has a minority stake in Championship side Wrexham, demonstrates that the capital markets think City are imperilled, with the appeal process by no means straightforward.

It has been revealed that if an appeal failed, City could seek a judicial review of the commission's findings at the High Court. But to do so, they would need to demonstrate that the Premier League acted outside its powers or reached a conclusion which no reasonable authority could have reached. City would need the High Court’s permission to make a judicial review application and the bar is high.

Financial analyst Paul Quinn wrote on The Esk website that Apollo’s concern had been with City, not Abu Dhabi itself. Three weeks ago, Apollo agreed to take a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Sheikh Mansour and run by City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. Apollo and City have not commented.

Quinn stated that CFG needed the money because it was not self-funding, despite City’s financial strength. CFG’s pre-tax loss widened from £122.2m to £292.3m in the last financial year. City produced £694.1m of CFG’s £888m group revenue and ran up a £9m loss.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal Women missed the chance to end their frustrating run of draws at home as London City Lionesses came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw at the Emirates Stadium.

Sources indicate that frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in an exciting start to the game. But Isobel Goodwin equalised almost straight away. Despite creating plenty of chances, Renée Slegers’ side failed to find a second goal.

According to recent reports, arsenal have now lost their last five WSL games at the Emirates. The results were yet another frustrating afternoon for the defending champions, who put in a strong display against Barcelona in Europe earlier in the week.

Sources indicate that arsenal started on a high note, creating some dangerous chances with their quick play. Emily Fox and Lisa Baum worked really well together down the right, and Ona Batlle had a great chance from the edge of the box.

As the pressure mounted, Fox surged forward and played a perfectly weighted through ball to Alessia Russo. The striker turned and played the ball back to Maanum, who rounded off her impressive comeback from injury by finishing.

Arsenal had little time to rejoice. London City equalised just a minute later as Goodwin found herself in space to fire past Misa Rodríguez.

The visitors looked more confident after equalising, but Mary Earps was proving a tough ask for Arsenal to score past. The ex-Manchester United shot-stopper kept out Baum and made some key stops from Arsenal’s efforts.

Rodriguez also had to make a key stop before half-time as she got a hand to Daniela Arques Lazaro’s powerful strike to keep the scores level.

The Gunners continued their attacking play but were made to work hard by a high pressing side from London City.

In a recent development, but Arsenal still managed to create some chances. Caitlin Foord put Earps under pressure and Maanum and Baum combined before the latter saw her curl just wide.

According to recent reports, london City posed a threat too. With Kadidiatou Diani and Grace Geyoro causing defensive problems for Arsenal, Geyoro fired into the side netting.

In a recent development, delphine Cascarino had the game’s defining moment of the second half, hitting the crossbar from outside the box. However, Arsenal were lucky to escape and Maanum came close to winning the game, hitting the woodwork from a dangerous counter.

Slegers brought on Kyra Cooney-Cross and Olivia Smith in the 72nd minute to provide some latest energy. Smith looked lively upon entering the game, but Earps denied her efforts and Batlle’s cross.

Emily Fox had to be substituted due to injury in the final moments of the game, but Slegers later indicated that she would be okay.

It has been revealed that the Gunners were unable to find a winning goal and will now turn their attention to their Champions League clash on Thursday with Lyon. They will then face West Ham at home in the WSL.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Expected Goals is widely agreed to be the best way of measuring how well Premier League clubs play in any particular game.
  • To get a better look at how sides are doing, the Expected Goals (xG) metric allows you to get a better picture of just how teams are performing.
  • Expected goals (xG) is a statistic used to work out how many goals should be scored in a match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Expected Goals is widely agreed to be the best way of measuring how well Premier League clubs play in any particular game.

To get a better look at how sides are doing, the Expected Goals (xG) metric allows you to get a better picture of just how teams are performing.

Expected goals (xG) is a statistic used to work out how many goals should be scored in a match.

With every single shot awarded an xG value based on the difficulty of the attempt, with factors including distance from goal, type of shot and number of defenders present affecting the value.

The higher the xG of a particular shot, the more likely a goal should be scored from that shot.

The xG value of every shot in a game is then used to calculate the expected goals in a particular match.

So rather than just the usual basic statistics of how many shots each team has, Expected Goals factors in where shots were taken from and how good a chance was and whether defenders in the way etc.

These Expected Goals stats from Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2.

Newcastle United 1.73 Arsenal 1.48.

As you can see, Newcastle’s Expected Goals stat is higher than Arsenal’s by a decent degree. Not a huge difference but a clear one.

When you look at the other stats below, they back up the fact that Newcastle United deserved at the very least a point AND arguably if either side deserved to have won the game, it was United, as they had the better chances overall.

As well as the higher Expected Goals stat, Newcastle had twice as many corners (6 v 3), whilst the overall shots (12 v 13) and efforts on target (3 v 4) were almost identical.

The England international has reportedly signed a newly introduced five-year deal which will keep him at the Emirates Stadium until 2031. The contract is a reward for the midfielder who has been instrumental in Arsenal’s success since he moved to the club in 2023 from West Ham.

According to recent reports, rice has not just provided the presence and protection that Arsenal were hoping for with their £105 million signing. He has continued to develop his game, especially after returning to his deeper midfield role this season.

Rice came in as a defensive midfielder, but Arteta swiftly saw how much he could offer higher up the park.

His physicality, ability to run into the box and set piece threat made him a useful left-sided number eight. Rice had a huge impact in midfield for Arsenal, bringing goals and a newly introduced attacking threat.

But Rice has played in a more advanced position on the right-hand side of the midfield duo this season, and this has not limited his impact but instead highlighted another key part of his game.

Rice has made the most line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season, with Opta stats reported by Sky Sports showing he is second only to Premier League players.

This is of particular interest, as he has often come under criticism for his distribution. But he is averaging nearly double the amount of line-breaking passes he did last season.

While his running ability is still an asset, he is also becoming much better at penetrating through the defensive lines to find his teammates, giving Arsenal another option to move the ball forward with.

The development of Rice is key in securing a new contract at Arsenal.

The 27-year-old has already proven to be one of the most reliable members of Arteta’s squad and has shown great longevity by only missing five games out of his 119 Premier League outings in his first spell at the club.

Former West Ham teammate Jack Wilshere has also praised Rice’s strong work ethic, ability to adapt and natural leadership qualities.

It has been revealed that the reported 5-year deal will keep Rice at Arsenal until 2031, into his early 30s. While the terms of the deal have yet to be signed, it is a huge statement from the club.

They are not only rewarding Rice for what he has done but also investing in what he can do.

With Arteta finding new ways to utilise Rice’s qualities in midfield, Rice could still have some of his best years ahead of him.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We asked Davey Hat-Trick to give us his match ratings and player comments after Newcastle 2 Arsenal 2 in the Premier League.
  • Recent findings suggest that out of the 1,000+ games I have watched in person, the 4-4 draw with Arsenal 15 years ago is the match that most deserves the ‘game of two halves’ label.
  • Industry observers note that A blind man could have seen the gulf in class between the two sides in the first half.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We asked Davey Hat-Trick to give us his match ratings and player comments after Newcastle 2 Arsenal 2 in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that out of the 1,000+ games I have watched in person, the 4-4 draw with Arsenal 15 years ago is the match that most deserves the ‘game of two halves’ label. This one – against the same opponents – wasn’t far off.

Industry observers note that A blind man could have seen the gulf in class between the two sides in the first half. Arsenal outclassed Newcastle without trying. Newcastle looked petrified, and it looked like no one wanted the ball. Having said that, Arsenal only scored a single goal, and didn’t really come that close again. Our centre halves were good.

The second half could not have been more different. Newcastle tore into Arsenal from the get-go, and the Gunners looked shell-shocked. By the time Arsenal had recovered their composure, Newcastle were 2-1 up. In my opinion, we were playing as well as we had all season.

Sources indicate that arsenal were bound to come back into it, and they did. They scored an equaliser, but that’s not to say Newcastle were overwhelmed. We were giving as good as we got, and continued to do so.

Having conceded, most Geordies were fearing the traditional last-minute winner for our opponents, and when the officials came up with nine minutes of injury time, it seemed nailed on.

But Newcastle held firm, and got a deserved point against the reigning champions, and this season’s most likely winners. It was a triumph of belief, effort, teamwork and quality, and it had a galvanising effect on the black and white faithful. St James’ Park was rocking to a degree I haven’t witnessed since our opener against Liverpool.

In a recent development, it’s hard to give the players a sensible mark. Everyone was poor in the first half. Everyone was excellent in the second.

Lukáš Horníček 5 Not at fault for Arsenal’s first, may have done better for their second, but he always looked nervy and unsure with the ball at his feet. His distribution was poor and he never looked confident.

In a recent development, amar Dedić 4 Good player, bad game. Stranded for Arsenal’s first and took a pointless yellow card way before half time. Subbed off at half time, a bold move by the manager, but the correct one.

According to recent reports, malick Thiaw 8 If it wasn’t for our centre halves, Arsenal could have been 3-0 up at half time. Their challenges, blocks and clearances kept Newcastle in the game. Just. The second half saw Thiaw liberated to pick his passes, get up the pitch and score Newcastle’s second from all of four inches.

In a recent development, dan Burn 8 A captain’s innings. Kept the Gunners from tearing us apart in the first half and made a nuisance of himself in attack in the second. I thought he wouldn’t get much game time this campaign. Now he’s one of the first names on the team sheet.

Lewis Hall 6 People – me included – were calling him the best left back in the world this week. I still think he is…but he wasn’t anything like that in that first half. Was mugged for Arsenal’s first and made a few other errors. He typified Newcastle’s second half – a much improved performance. Got up the pitch and had Arsenal on the back foot. Went off with what looked like a strain. Let’s hope it’s nothing serious.

Sean Steur 5 The game passed him by in the first half and he didn’t appear for the second. I don’t think he was bad, just not particularly effective.

Lewis Miley 6 A mate of mine thinks he was our best player. I just thought it was a decent game from Lewis. Not exactly dominant, but decent on the ball, and another wiho improved in the second half. Had a run at goal which nearly came off.

Jacob Murphy 5 I only remember Newcastle having one attempt in the first half and it was Murphy who had it. It was on target as well, except it hit his own team-mate. Other than that, Jacob offered little else and was hooked at half time.

Joe Willock 6 He’d be on a 7 or 8 if he got his head up and passed the ball instead of taking on ridiculous long distance shots. I thought he had a decent game, to be fair, and was full of energy. It looked to me like he played deeper in the second half and it worked. I think he got a dodgy assist for Thiaw’s goal.

Sources indicate that harvey Barnes 8 Another who seemed like a bystander in the first half but who came to life in the second. Scored the goal that gave us belief and even went past his man a few times on the wing. Well played lad.

William Osula 6.5 There will be some who say Osula ‘did nowt’ in the first half but I think that was due to his team-mates being pinned back in their own half. He was isolated, although he highlighted his usual willingness to run. Second half was a different game. His colleagues actually got up the pitch to support him and he looked much better. A good assist for our first goal and it became a more confident display.

Tino Livramento 7 I’d forgotten what an excellent footballer Tino can be. He came on for the second half and looked like the player we saw two seasons ago. Quick, intelligent and good on the ball. It’s fair to say the half-time substitutes improved the team; none more than Tino.

According to recent reports, anthony Elanga 5.5 To be truthful, he didn’t do a lot with the ball that I remember, but he did inject pace and energy, qualities that were non-existent first half. We looked a different team. We were a different team.

Jacob Ramsey 6 We looked more secure when Jacob entered the fray. Suddenly our midfield looked better than Arsenal’s. Played some good balls but skied a shot that could have won us the game.

Yoane Wissa 4 On for a tiring Willock. Found it difficult to get into the game.

Recent findings suggest that sven Botman 5 Came on at a time when most fans’ hearts were in their mouths – Arsenal were looking dangerous. But Sven held his own and looked the part. Relief all round.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The second international break of the season is upon us, which is a good time to take stock of how things are going beyond he men’s first team.

An ownership and management should not just be judged on one area of the club, but rather multiple different departments. The youth sector needs to be developing players in the right way, while the rising prevalence of women’s football gives added impetus to make the Femminile side as competitive as possible.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that that being mentioned, can be hard enough keeping up with how the senior team are doing without thinking about the various other sides operating under the Milan umbrella. So, we have provided a summary of how Milan Futuro, Milan Primavera and Milan Women are doing so far in 2026-27.

It was all change over the summer for the Futuro as they brought in Sergio Navarro as the head coach. The idea was to create some continuity with Ruben Amorim’s more continental style of football, and the pedigree that the Spaniard has suggested it was a positive move.

While not a necessity, the objective for the campaign will no doubt have been set as competing for promotion back to the third tier, which is the level that the project started at prior to the relegation in 2024-25.

Position: It is a case of so far, so good for Navarro’s men. They sit fourth in the standings with 23 points from 11 games, obtained through seven wins, two draws and two losses. They have scored 21 goals (third-most in the league) and allowed 15.

It has been revealed that importantly, the Futuro have a game in hand on the sides above them. If they win it they would go level with Chievo Verona (yes, that Chievo) and Nibbiano & Valtidone who are on 26 points. The former, however, have a 10 better goal difference.

The U23s are part of the Premier League International Cup and they got past Everton 2-1 in the first game, with matches against Stoke later this month and Tottenham in November to come, both away from home.

Industry observers note that high point: On October 18, Milan’s second team went to the current league-leaders Chievo and beat them 2-1, with Bonomi scoring a late winner. That was an early marker of what this team are capable of. A special mention must go to the Premier League Cup win at Goodison Park against Everton, too.

Industry observers note that low point: That aforementioned win in Verona came in the round after Milan had lost 2-1 at home to Rovato Vertovese. They are a side that have only won twice all season and currently occupy the relegation spots, so it was a big blow before a big response.

It has been revealed that key players: There have been multiple players that have stood out. Levin Asanji has scored four goals in the league, as has Lorenzo Ossolo. Fabio Pandolfi has been playing a deeper midfield role and looks to have quality well beyond his 18 years of age, with three goals to his name.

Silvano Vos is having a resurgence, while the likes of Emanuele Sala, Mattia Cappelletti, Alessandro Bonomi and Emanuele Borsani have all started every single game, aiding their development under the new coach. El Hadji Malick Cisse – a January arrival – is also turning a lot of heads.

For a bit more deeper reading on the tactical approach used by Milan Futuro under Navarro, we suggest reading the analysis we put out over the international break.

The 2025-26 season was a mixed one for the Primavera side, as their record of 11 wins and 11 defeats in 38 games shows perfectly. They finished 11th, nine points off the relegation play-offs but 10 points off the Scudetto play-offs, though a lot of the younger talents had been again accelerated into the Futuro side.

Giovanni Renna remained at the helm going into the newly introduced campaign, the coach that has been promoted up the ranks and thus knows a lot of the players. The hope was that continuity would yield better results, and so far it has.

Position: At the time of writing, the U20 side are sixth in the Primavera 1 league, which puts them in a final play-off spot. They have won five of their first 10 games but they have also lost four, so they remain a bit of a rollercoaster ride of inconsistency.

Looking upwards, Parma are currently top on 21 points, but the Rossoneri are within striking distance of Inter, who are in second on 19 points. However, Renna’s side are also a bad round away from being in the bottom half too.

Industry observers note that milan Primavera progressed in the Coppa Italia Primavera at the end of October, beating Catanzaro 2-1 thanks to a late winner from Dotta. Como are the opponents in the next round.

In a recent development, high point: It’s hard to look past the last two rounds in truth. The Primavera seem to have really clicked, scoring 10 goals in the last 180 minutes of action, beating Monza 5-0 away from home and then AlbinoLeffe 5-1 at home.

An honourable mention must go to the 2-0 win over Juventus in September, given they are in a similar position with also having a B-team (Juve Next Gen), so they will continue to serve as a useful point of comparison.

Low point: Back on October 10, the young Diavoli lost 2-0 against Atalanta which was their third league defeat in a row. There was talk of crisis mode as the slide down the table continued, and against an Atalanta side that are now third-bottom of the league. Thankfully, they turned it around swiftly.

Key players: A bit like with the Futuro, the goals have been shared around the Milan Primavera squad. Mattia Zaramella has emerged recently as a star with four goals, as has Max Anastasio who arrived from Bologna and has the same amount.

Recent findings suggest that then, Andrea Cullotta (a centre-back), Vincent Ibrahimovic (a midfielder) and Edoardo Tartaglia (a full-back) all have two goals. Renna has called upon the same core group of players largely. Matteo Geroli, Francesco Domnitei, Cullotta, Zaramella, Tartaglia, Anastasio and Yanis Massaouadi have all appeared in every round.

Industry observers note that last season was not one that Milan Women will want to shout about, given that they finished sixth in the table and seven points off the play-off spots in the end. They won just nine of 22 games, placing them below even Fiorentina and Lazio, plus Juventus, city rivals Inter and eventual champions Roma.

However, like with the Primavera, consistency was the name of the game. So, Suzanne Bakker remained as the head coach, and there wasn’t as much player turnover as in some recent years.

Industry observers note that position: There have only been seven rounds so far in Serie A Femminile, but the Rossonere have got off to a stuttering start. They have just seven points from their opening seven games, which puts them in eighth place in the table. They have scored 11 goals but let in a joint-league-high 16.

Industry observers note that looking upwards, Roma lead the way with 21 points having won every game. Inter are second on 16 points – so nine more than Milan – while Juventus occupy the final play-off spot on 12. Over their shoulders, Sassuolo are in bottom (the only relegation spot), with three points.

In the Women’s Cup, Milan drew 1-1 with Como, beat Como 1907 (affiliated with the men’s team presently in Serie A, the others are a stand-alone club) 2-1, and then lost 1-0 to Juventus to end their campaign.

High point: This one is quite an easy pick, and it has to be the 2-1 victory over Juventus last month. Thea Kyvåg and Monica Renzotti overturned Lenzini’s opener, which had come with just under a quarter of an hour left on the clock, engineering a late comeback that sparked jubilant scenes.

Low point: The tone for what has been a disappointing campaign so far for Bakker’s ladies was set in round one, when they were beaten 4-1 by Como 1907. Then, losing 1-0 away at Como was another dark day, given they have only won twice.

On November 7, the 3-0 derby defeat to Inter – which included a red card for Milan – served only to highlight the big gulf between the two teams at the moment.

Key players: Christy Grimshaw remains the shining light for Milan Women, with three goals and an assist to her name. The scoring charts then see Sara Stokic on three goals, with Sara Fornes, Park Soojeong and Monica Renzotti all netting twice.

Grimshaw is one of three players to start every game so far under Bakker, with the others being defenders Angelica Soffia and Nerea Nevado. Sandra Estevez has emerged as the number one between the sticks too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal are continuing their excellent work in retaining their key players as David Raya and Jurrien Timber have both been approached about new contracts.

Industry observers note that this comes after Declan Rice signed a five-year contract extension. The midfielder will now stay at the Emirates until 2031, but Mikel Arteta is now close to locking down more defenders in his squad.

Timber has reportedly agreed better terms, and Raya is also on the verge of a fresh deal. Although both deals are yet to be officially confirmed, it shows how important Arsenal are trying to keep them at the top.

The importance of retaining Raya and Timber is evident.

According to recent reports, since arriving at the club from Brentford, Raya has become Arteta’s first choice in goal. He has become an important part of Arsenal’s attacking play due to his distribution, decision-making and game under pressure.

His performances have also earned him honours outside of North London as he was named in the 2026 FIFPRO World 11. Only the second Arsenal player to win the award after Thierry Henry in 2006.

Sources indicate that raya has a contract in place until 2028, although he was given better financial terms last year. However, a new long-term deal will offer more security to one of Arteta’s most trusted players.

Since joining from Ajax in 2023, Timber has become a key part of Arsenal’s backline. Despite injury problems, he has proven to be one of the most dependable defenders in the squad.

It has been revealed that he can play as a right back, left back and centre back which provides Arteta with great versatility. He has the physicality and technical ability to help Arsenal at both ends of the pitch.

It has been reported that Timber has agreed to better terms. How long his contract is for is unknown.

There is a pattern beginning to emerge from Arsenal’s recent contract news.

Recent findings suggest that rice has been signed until 2031. Timber is also expected to sign, committing his peak years to the club. Raya is also expected to sign soon, with talks remarked to be at an advanced stage.

Sources indicate that arteta recently signed a contract extension until 2030. They aren’t just trying to keep their best players for another year but are looking to create consistency within the squad and management.

This is an matter for any club competing within the domestic and European leagues, as it can cause problems with team cohesion and development due to constant change of key players.

While there is still work to be done, this is positive news for fans.

It has been revealed that signing Raya and Timber will ensure that two key components of Arteta’s backline are safe. It will also show that with Rice’s new contract, they’re looking to build on their recent success and not let their best players near the end of their contracts.

Arsenal are noted to be trying to reward Piero Hincapié with better contract terms after just months since making his move permanent.

In a recent development, according to reports, negotiations are at an advanced stage between the Ecuadorian and international players. David Raya is also near to signing a new contract as Mikel Arteta looks to retain his key squad members.

Sources indicate that however, Hincapié is in a slightly different position compared to his teammates. The 24-year-old only signed a five-year deal permanently in the summer.

Recent findings suggest that therefore, he could be discussing an increase in his salary rather than an extension. It has not been officially confirmed by either Arsenal or the player.

Arsenal have exercised their option to make Hincapié’s loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent.

The defender made 39 appearances in all competitions during his first season in North London, scoring one goal and providing two assists. He has become an crucial part of Arteta’s defensive options.

His versatility has been an asset to Arsenal. His ability to play as a centre-back or left-back meaning he provides another option to utilise when problems occur with injuries or rotation in defence.

However, Hincapié has been overshadowed by Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori, making it a tough battle for playing time.

In a recent development, in the current campaign, he has played just five games in the league, with all of them coming off the bench. A total of 67 minutes has been played.

Hincapié will not be too concerned by this, as Arsenal have plenty of defensive options, and he provides cover in two positions.

The news that Hincapié is in talks is part of a bigger story around the club trying to keep their best players.

Declan Rice has signed a fresh five-year deal with Jurrien Timber, signing on improved terms. Raya is also stated to be close to signing a new deal.

According to recent reports, arteta has already signed his future to the club until 2030. It is clear that they want to keep the continuity going forward after recent success.

While Hincapié has a contract until next year, renegotiating his deal would show how much Arsenal values him.

They may want to reward their players who have promptly become key members of their squad.

He has no reports of being unhappy and looking to leave the club. It seems he is being rewarded for his contributions to the club and to give him security in the long term.

This is a huge vote of confidence for a player who has only just completed his permanent move this summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham’s familiar profligacy in front of goal came back to haunt them, as did their propensity to go behind in the first half of games as the points were shared at London Stadium this afternoon.

Sources indicate that from Preston’s first corner, the fanbase was understandably apprehensive, knowing West Ham’s weaknesses from dead balls earlier in the season. Again the curse struck, with Piroe heading the ball over his own oncoming goal keeper’s fists, the ball then looping onto the post and allowing a gentle tap-in for Preston to take the lead.

Herrick rallied well after conceding early.

According to recent reports, the wheels could have come off for West Ham’s young goal keeper at that point: However, all credit to Herrick. It would have been very easy for his confidence to crumble after that early combi-cock-up, but he rallied well and even appeared to be smiling as the game went on, with several catches and a couple of really good saves surely meaning the shirt is his for the time being.

West Ham hit the post four times during a frenetic period in the first half when their intensity was high, but it seemed as though the ball simply would not go between the posts.

It has been revealed that familiar problems surfaced in the second half as the pace dropped and West Ham ran out of ideas, notably after Austbø had been substituted. Manor Solomon, looking very one-footed, simply ran inside and passed square. Frustratingly, the game slowed in pace in the last twenty minutes with the Hammers looking devoid of new ideas just at the time when they should have been upping the tempo.

It is clear that there’s still a shortage of pace in this side and with a build up that got slower as the game went on, West Ham’s bench looked as if it desperately needed an injection of Antonio-like pace to scare opponents and perhaps take on a shot!

A disappointment for the West Ham supporters, who booed their team off in the now time-honoured tradition as another two points went west. Against the bottom side.

And so it came to pass with Bruno Guimaraes… Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The reaction to the departure of Bruno Guimaraes seems to have overshadowed that of Alexander Isak.
  • Fans had assumed the Brazilian’s deep connection with the United faithful was mutual, so discovering it was a bit more one-sided than anyone believed, only heightened the sense of betrayal when he left for the Emirates.
  • Some writers on The Mag were asked for 50 words on Bruno Guimaraes ahead of this match; most accepting that he’s still a legend, but that the manner of his departure left a sour taste such that he shouldn’t have been immune to a tempestuous reception.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The reaction to the departure of Bruno Guimaraes seems to have overshadowed that of Alexander Isak.

Fans had assumed the Brazilian’s deep connection with the United faithful was mutual, so discovering it was a bit more one-sided than anyone believed, only heightened the sense of betrayal when he left for the Emirates.

Some writers on The Mag were asked for 50 words on Bruno Guimaraes ahead of this match; most accepting that he’s still a legend, but that the manner of his departure left a sour taste such that he shouldn’t have been immune to a tempestuous reception.

And so it came to pass; Guimaraes was roundly booed and jeered, with both his greed and his parentage loudly called into question, which felt a touch ironic, given how the faithful had once adored his father, a man who used to sit in the away end and soak up the adulation.

As it happens, Bruno was largely anonymous and replaced by the more energetic Lewis-Skelly when his side was trailing, although he hadn’t been far from converting a Declan Rice cross in the 28th minute, something that would have amounted to a low blow for most of the 52,661 crowd had his effort found its way into the back of the net.

That chance came just before Arsenal’s dominance saw them ahead. Kai Havertz dispossessed Lewis Hall high up the pitch and slid a sublime pass to Eberechi Eze, who whipped the ball past Lukas Hornicek.

Newcastle were struggling and it was what I’d expected, pre-match bonhomie with old friends and the lad, fueled by some decent ale, had quickly evaporated when the team was unveiled.

Right on half-time, Madueke, who had already hit the base of the post in the sixth minute, passed up a golden opportunity to double Arsenal’s lead, as some of the boos that had been reserved for Bruno were now being directed at those in the black and white.

Thank goodness Matthias Jaissle had both seen enough and managed to hold his nerve, a decisive triple substitution that introduced Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey, and Anthony Elanga into the fray proving transformational.

According to recent reports, just four minutes after the restart, Joe Willock pressed Martin Odegaard into a costly mistake on the Arsenal left. Will Osula scooped up the loose ball and teed up Harvey Barnes, who fired clinically past David Raya to register United’s first home strike in over two months.

Barnes will tear you apart echoed around the stadium, Dedic unable to join in with the bow and arrow celebrations, Livramento now doing a better job at right back, whilst Ramsey had shored up the midfield as Steur’s replacement and Elanga looked a whole lot better than the lethargic Murphy.

Energised by a crowd that was itself suitably invigorated, United turned the game on its head.

Sources indicate that in the 62nd minute, Lewis Hall’s corner was nodded back across goal by an unmarked Dan Burn. This sparked a frenetic goalmouth scramble that ended with Malick Thiaw poking home from close range, a goal confirmed after an agonising VAR check that looked at supposed handball and offside offences, that feeling of dread never materialising as Chris Kavanagh finally signalled the goal would stand.

At this stage, United were very much on top but just couldn’t muster that elusive third, and when David Raya left the field following a collision with Osula in the 70th minute, rather than worsen the Gunners evening, the long break before Kepa Arrizabalaga replaced his compatriot allowed them to regroup and turn the tide.

I’d noted to the lad that this was going to be a long twenty minutes, possibly half an hour, for us to negotiate and somewhat inevitably, Arsenal hit us on the counter in the 78th minute.

Recent findings suggest that released down the flank by Odegaard, Noni Madueke cut inside to drill a shot that squirmed through Hornicek’s grasp to level the scores. Could he have saved it? Maybe, all that good work at Craven Cottage a fortnight ago undone in an instant.

At this point, had anyone feared an Arsenal winner was coming, that might have been justified, they are a very good team and their substitutions demonstrated a squad that has strength in depth.

But the final stages, including nine minutes of added time, saw both sides pushing for a winner and it’s Newcastle that will feel more aggrieved, first Kepa denied Lewis Miley before Havertz nearly scored an own goal, the crossbar coming to his rescue as the spoils were shared.

Industry observers note that I wrote an article for The Mag recently highlighting that United had picked up five more points from their opening ten fixtures when making a comparison with the same fixtures from the previous campaign. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

It has been revealed that he was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

It has been revealed that storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

It has been revealed that storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

It has been revealed that storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

Recent findings suggest that he played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Recent findings suggest that following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

It has been revealed that he will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

'If you don't give him what he wants, he'll burn your house down': Inside the 'cult' of Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as sources from his crumbling sporting empire reveal the destructive know-it-all arrogance of Man United co-owner and his henchmen

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that the flat rural acres of the Turweston Aerodrome, in the north-west corner of Buckinghamshire, are far enough from human habitation for anyone padlocked in a building out there to feel seriously threatened.
  • The ‘imprisonment’ of the four-time British Olympic champion in a building, with signs declaring ‘No Entry’ fixed to the external doors, was one of the more extraordinary allegations to emerge from the court case, settled this week, over a £180million yacht Ratcliffe and Ainslie built together for the 2024 America’s Cup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 12:11 EST, 19 November 2026.

It has been revealed that the flat rural acres of the Turweston Aerodrome, in the north-west corner of Buckinghamshire, are far enough from human habitation for anyone padlocked in a building out there to feel seriously threatened. And if the testimony of Sir Ben Ainslie is to be believed, that’s what can come of crossing swords with Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The ‘imprisonment’ of the four-time British Olympic champion in a building, with signs declaring ‘No Entry’ fixed to the external doors, was one of the more extraordinary allegations to emerge from the court case, settled this week, over a £180million yacht Ratcliffe and Ainslie built together for the 2024 America’s Cup.

Ratcliffe, who had withdrawn financial support, was demanding the team’s assets and intellectual property, and, according to court papers, Ineos representative Raymond Fellows, assisted by two security contractors, arrived at the offices of Ainslie's Athena Racing and applied his own chain and padlock. He’d been refused the keys by the building’s owner. Ainslie and his financial officer Matt Robinson managed to leave the building through the fire escape.

Ineos were applying petrochemicals business methods to sport, as usual. Fellows had also been employed by Ratcliffe to provide security assistance amid protests at Ineos’ controversial British fracking sites. The experienced security industry executive observed that ‘a small hard core group of activists’ was at work and that social media surveillance was useful, according to court papers from an earlier case.

Ineos denied the ‘false imprisonment’ of Ainslie, insisting that their employee had padlocked the building to prevent anyone entering, not knowing that someone was inside and that, in any case, there were ‘alternative exit routes’.

Recent findings suggest that but the company did not entirely challenge Ainslie’s claim that Rob Nevin, chairman of Ratcliffe’s sports division and a Manchester United board member, had told him during a heated meeting about the disputed boat in Barcelona: ‘We have a phrase at Ineos: scorched earth. It means that if you don’t give Jim what he wants, he will burn your house down, or words to that effect.’.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe's relationship with his one-time friend Ben Ainslie ruptured after Ineos withdrew support for the latter's America’s Cup bid.

Ratcliffe's running of Manchester United is criticised by one anonymous source. ‘People like him see football on TV and just assume they can do it,’ they say.

That threat, which Ineos say was only made figuratively, illustrates how Ratcliffe runs his businesses with what several sources describe as a cult-like authority, full of such maxims and mantras laid down to staff who fear him.

That ‘cult of Sir Jim’ is born of the billionaire’s own immense air of superiority and is something he seems to have instilled in some of his most senior executives.

Nevin, 68, a long-standing Ratcliffe lieutenant, has informed some who have encountered him since he arrived at Old Trafford that he has completed 60 or more major ‘transactions’ – business deals – in the oil and gas industry. He is described as ‘not short on confidence’.

Recent findings suggest that nevin chairs Ineos Sport, the collection of acquisitions built up when Ratcliffe believed his firm could straddle multiple sports and succeed at all of them, in the style of Red Bull. Ratcliffe disastrously installed his brother, Bob, as chief executive at OGC Nice, the second of the football teams he bought, and that air of superiority and ‘always knowing’ has been manifest at United, too.

Ratcliffe demonstrated to some of the Manchester United players the stretches he was using for London Marathon training, after buying the club. He considered his friend Sir Dave Brailsford to be ‘best in class’ when it came to running the football side of the club, despite the former Team Sky cycling chief only having a loose connection of football contacts, mostly picked up from his appearances on the Leaders in Sport conference circuit for his friend Jimmy Worrall, the entrepreneur who set up that business.

Sources have told us that Brailsford was so enamoured with Manchester City, after arriving to ‘save United’, that he and other Ineos people were ‘skipping around’ when Omar Berrada, chief operations officer at the Etihad, was hired as chief executive.

‘There was no sense from Ratcliffe of needing people who understand the industry and its craft,’ says one source, speaking on condition of anonymity. ‘People like this see football on TV and just assume they can do it.’.

Ratcliffe (pictured next to former United boss Erik ten Hag) inexplicably considered Dave Brailsford (right) to be ‘best in class’ when it came to running the football side of the club.

Rob Nevin (right) chairs Ineos Sport, the collection of acquisitions built up when Ratcliffe wrongly believed his firm could straddle multiple sports and succeed at all of them.

Recent findings suggest that none of Ratcliffe’s executives will be wanting to tell him that. A further sense of what a formidable presence he is for his own staff came in a 30-minute ‘Ask Jim’ interview with him, conducted by his own director of corporate affairs, Tom Crotty, this summer.

Ratcliffe stares at the floor for much of the time as Crotty bowls him a series of long-hop questions and he seems profoundly miserable, revealing little more than his unhappiness with the British government’s management of North Sea oilfields and his dislike for the British sports press.

Recent findings suggest that the interview was conducted the day after the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina in July, which Ratcliffe attended. ‘It was fabulous. A great celebration, despite the whining British press who really didn’t like it,’ he says.

Sources indicate that asked how he switches off, he cites time on the golf driving range and fishing on his salmon farm in Iceland – to which Berrada and the Glazers have had to make their way for some executive meetings. ‘Biggest lessons learned in 2025?’ There don’t appear to have been any. At no stage do United feature.

Ratcliffe trots out his extremely well-worn mantra about the major three traits Ineos prize most – ‘Grit, rigour, humour’ – informing the relentlessly positive Crotty of the need to ‘do work properly before you make crucial decisions, because you need to spend capital well.’.

In a recent development, that’s not happened in sport. The extraordinary rupture with Ainslie, after Ineos withdrew support for a third America’s Cup cycle and he continued to use the boat, is part of a general, hugely acrimonious winding down of the Ineos Sport masterplan.

OGC Nice and FC Lausanne-Sport, Ratcliffe’s European football clubs, are up for sale amid fan protest, while it is widely expected that Ineos will eventually disappear from cycling. They have already diluted their involvement, with the team formerly known as the Ineos Grenadiers now co-sponsored by Danish technology firm Netcompany. The All Blacks and Tottenham Hotspur both sued Ineos for prematurely terminating commercial relationships. Both parties ultimately reached a confidential legal settlement with the manufacturer.

What United need, as they look to Mauricio Pochettino for deliverance, is for Ratcliffe to climb down from his lofty peak, display some of the humility which has been missing and admit there have been faults.

What United need, as they look to Mauricio Pochettino for deliverance, is for Ratcliffe to display some humility.

The club's executives, including CEO Omar Berrada (centre) and director of football Jason Wilcox (right), have appeared out of their depth and in need of support.

In a recent development, the view among some outsiders who interact at a high level with the club is, in the words of one, that United are ‘the biggest club in the world and yet no longer the biggest club in the world'. They carry huge expectation, yet are unable to compete for transfer fees and wages with Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City, and have removed excellent staff without replacing them. To cite only one, Victoria Timpson secured the club’s lucrative Snapdragon sponsorship deal but still departed.

‘If United were an iPhone, someone would need to unfold the paper clip pretty quick, push it in the side of the phone and hard restart everything,’ notes the aforementioned source. 'The club need a genuinely industry-leading chief executive, a sporting director of the calibre of Edwin van der Sar who, unlike Jason Wilcox, has the experience, pedigree and knowledge he accumulated as CEO at Ajax. They need a boardroom presence and link to the fans like Bryan Robson.'.

Ratcliffe does not even sit on the United board himself, leaving it to Nevin and John Reece, one of the Ineos co-founders.

Another of his Ineos appointees was the 63-year-old Frenchman Jean-Claude Blanc, an experienced statesman and marketeer with an Olympic, Tour de France and PSG background, who is described as pleasant and without ego – though he was supposedly in the room when the 'scorched' earth comment was made to Ainslie. Blanc was recruited for his gravitas, rather than to pull up trees. He has stepped down from United's board.

Ainslie and Ratcliffe are no longer thought to be friends. Shortly before the alleged episode in the locked aerodrome building, Ainslie observed, in relation to Ratcliffe, that there was a difference between business and sport, where teams were delicately balanced, nuanced groups of people.

According to recent reports, ‘You want to save money and be efficient, but you’ve got to make sure you look after people. You need that balance,’ he mentioned. Under the terms of the court settlement, Ainslie gets to keep the boat and sail off into the sunset, leaving Ratcliffe to whatever storms come next.
